summary.headline: UNO Minda Q2 FY27 revenue rose 38% YoY to Rs 6,655 crore and PAT 38% to Rs 420 crore, with management holding FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 11% ±50 bps.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations reached Rs 6,655 crore in Q2 FY27, up 38% YoY, with EBITDA up 33% to Rs 733 crore at an 11% margin. PAT attributable to shareholders grew 38% to Rs 420 crore. Growth was led by casting (+57%), green mobility (+102%), switches (+37%) and lighting (+25%), with management citing capacity commissioning at alloy wheels and HPDC at Bawal/Bauer. Net debt rose to Rs 2,412 crore from Rs 2,179 crore at March 31, 2026, while management reported H1 free cash flow of Rs 404 crore. Management reiterated the full-year margin guidance despite commodity pass-through being margin-dilutive.

financial_highlights.value: Rs 2,412 crore; net debt to equity 0.31
financial_highlights.change: Up from Rs 2,179 crore at Mar 31, 2026

financial_highlights.value: 20.7% reported; 24.6% excluding CWIP and land bank

segments.name: Switches
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 1,609 crore, +37% YoY, about 24% of group revenue; exports grew significantly and the four-wheeler switch business reached Rs 617 crore (+430% YoY as stated). Shifting of operations to the new Faridabad facility is on track for completion this fiscal.

segments.name: Lighting
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 1,381 crore, +25% YoY, about 21% of group revenue; growth led by two-wheeler lighting and EV tooler OEMs, with new pixel-based headlamp and taillamp orders from a global PV OEM.

segments.name: Casting (alloy wheels, aluminium die casting)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 1,441 crore, +57% YoY, partly reflecting higher raw material prices. Alloy wheel capacity rose to 6.3 million wheels per annum, with a target of 9 million by year-end; HPDC facility at Bawal added about 1 million units with four of six lines running.

segments.name: Seating
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 476 crore, +34% YoY, about 7% of group revenue; new entry with an incumbent Japanese two-wheeler OEM and a bus passenger seat customer.

segments.name: Green mobility
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 649 crore, +102% YoY, about 10% of group revenue. Breakdown: EV systems Rs 247 crore, alternate fuels Rs 187 crore, auto-electronics Rs 156 crore, EV controllers Rs 44 crore (stated).

segments.name: Other products (sensors/ADAS, acoustics, blow moulding, non-EV controllers, etc.)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 1,099 crore, +17% YoY, about 17% of revenue; sensors and ADAS Rs 261 crore, acoustics Rs 225 crore, blow moulding Rs 134 crore, non-EV controllers Rs 89 crore.

segments.name: Aftermarket and SPD
segments.commentary: Aftermarket revenue Rs 387 crore (about 6% of revenue); combined aftermarket and SPD channel Rs 709 crore (about 10%). Industrial business about 9% of revenue; exports about Rs 218 crore vs Rs 123 crore a year earlier.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 11% ±50 bps retained, despite commodity pass-through being margin-dilutive as no gross-up is received.
Management expects industry growth momentum to continue in H2 FY27 despite higher base, supported by festive season, wedding season and launches.
Expects RM-to-sales ratio and other cost ratios to improve over time as new business is priced at higher raw material levels; operating leverage and cost initiatives are cited as margin drivers.
Expects some initial rise in employee cost and depreciation as 16 plants ramp up over the first two years; no significant structural increase expected thereafter.
Targets pre-tax EBIT of roughly 18-20% on new projects by the third full year of production; incremental asset turn initially 1.8-2.0x, rising with sustaining capex.
Capex pipeline around Rs 5,200-5,300 crore including projects announced today; Rs 1,415 crore in four projects approved in August 2026.
capex_capacity: Alloy wheel capacity at 6.3 million wheels per annum, rising to 9 million with the Kharkhoda/Bawal expansions and to about 9.5 million after two remaining HPDC lines at Bawal; about 11.8 million wheels with Carcosa and Hosur expansions.
HPDC facility at Bawal: four of six lines commissioned, adding about 1 million units; remaining two lines to follow.
Sunroof: Rs 85 crore additional capacity approved at Bawal, with phase one commissioning expected around end FY27 and the additional capacity in Q2 FY28.

Four projects approved in August 2026 totalling about Rs 1,415 crore: Hosur die casting (Rs 510 crore), Kharkhoda two-wheeler alloy wheel expansion (Rs 155 crore), Bangalore moulding expansion (Rs 80 crore), and a new TGJV facility (about Rs 670 crore).
TGJV commissioned a new manufacturing facility at Harohalli, Bangalore, which weighed on its profitability through fixed costs, depreciation and interest.
Switch operations shifting to expanded Faridabad facility, to be completed this fiscal; EV charger programmes expected to be commissioned in the coming quarter.
demand_pricing: Indian auto production in Q2 crossed 1.9 lakh units (stated), up about 18% YoY; domestic sales up 18.2% to 83.9 lakh units. Passenger vehicle production 16.6 lakh units, up 25%.
Passenger vehicle exports fell 5.2% to 2.9 lakh units on high base and West Asia logistics constraints; total vehicle exports rose 23.9% to about 20.8 lakh units.
EV penetration reached 8% in passenger vehicles (registrations about 1 lakh, roughly doubled); electric two-wheeler penetration crossed 11% with registrations up 91% to about 5.9 lakh.
Raw material headwind: commodity price impact on the aluminium business is about Rs 260-270 crore (stated); pass-through is margin-dilutive.
Management reported share gains in aluminium wheels (two-wheeler capacity, new Bawal plant) and in switches, partly aided by favourable customer mix.

qa_highlights.question: How will margins trend in H2 FY27 given expected softening in input costs, and how is ramp-up progressing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is holding FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 11% ±50 bps; input costs are passed through both ways, but the pass-through is margin-dilutive. The Carcosa plant is under execution and expected to commission by fiscal year-end; new customers are not named until product launch.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the alloy wheel and switches growth, and will operating leverage or gross margin drive margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Aluminium commodity impact is about Rs 260-270 crore; wallet-share gains came from new two-wheeler capacity and casting customer mix. Switch exports grew significantly. Management expects RM-to-sales to improve over time as new business is priced at current raw material levels, with both operating leverage and gross margin improvement as drivers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for employee cost and depreciation as new capacity comes online?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost was about 11.3% of sales versus a historical 12.5-13.5% range. Depreciation rate is contained; a Carcosa plant impacted about Rs 5 crore. Expect some increase as 16 plants ramp up, mainly in the first two years.

qa_highlights.question: What incremental revenue and ROCE can the capex pipeline deliver?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex pipeline is around Rs 5,200-5,300 crore including today's projects. Initial asset turn is 1.8-2.0x, rising with sustaining capex; target pre-tax ROCE on new projects is 18-20% by the third full year, with blended returns within the company's current range.

qa_highlights.question: A question on human rights was asked.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it had nothing to share on this, as it was unclear where the query originated.

risks_watch: Commodity (aluminium) cost pass-through remains margin-dilutive; FY27 margin guidance depends on RM-to-sales improvement.
Net debt increased to Rs 2,412 crore from Rs 2,179 crore since March 2026 as capex runs at about Rs 500 crore in H1 alongside a Rs 5,200-5,300 crore pipeline.
TGJV Harohalli start-up is weighing on JV profitability; share of JV profit flat at Rs 60 crore.
Ramp-up of new capacities (Bawal HPDC remaining lines, Carcosa, Hosur) and the associated initial rise in employee cost and depreciation.
Passenger vehicle exports fell 5.2% YoY amid West Asia logistics constraints; monitor H2 export recovery.
Management did not name new customers in the casting business; the pipeline cannot yet be verified.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, with specific numbers on capacity and segments. Cautious on margins, acknowledging commodity pass-through dilution while holding full-year guidance. Evasive on new customer names, citing confidentiality.

Hence the margin guidance what we are given at the beginning of the year of 11% plus minus 50.
So it is actually margin-dilutive. So despite that we are holding on to our margin guidance for the full year.

adds.what: Alloy wheel capacity to 9 million wheels per annum by year-end (from 6.3 million), via Kharkhoda/Bawal expansions
HPDC facility at Bawal: four of six lines commissioned, adding about 1 million units; remaining two lines to follow
Sunroof additional capacity at Bawal (Rs 85 crore approved), phase one around end FY27
Hosur die casting facility (Rs 510 crore approved Aug 2026)
Kharkhoda two-wheeler alloy wheel expansion (Rs 155 crore approved Aug 2026)

growth.why: Management held FY27 EBITDA margin guidance at 11% ±50 bps and expects H2 industry momentum, with no explicit revenue growth guidance; growth is backed by alloy wheel capacity moving from 6.3 to 9 million wheels, HPDC lines, and Rs 1,415 crore of projects approved in August 2026, though timing for the larger projects is not given.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: FY27 EBITDA margin held at 11% ±50 bps with Q2 at 11% (Rs 733 crore on Rs 6,655 crore), but aluminium commodity impact of Rs 260-270 crore is margin-dilutive with no gross-up, so expansion depends on RM-to-sales improving over time.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Alloy wheel capacity is going from 6.3 to 9 million wheels per annum by year-end, two HPDC lines at Bawal remain to follow, and sunroof phase one is due around end FY27, with 4 of 6 HPDC lines already running.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management expects industry momentum to continue in H2 FY27 after Q2 revenue rose 38% YoY to Rs 6,655 crore and Indian auto production rose about 18% YoY, though no explicit volume guidance was given.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Four projects totalling about Rs 1,415 crore were approved in August 2026 and the pipeline is Rs 5,200-5,300 crore including today's announcements, with H1 capex around Rs 500 crore.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held rather than raised FY27 margin guidance, and gave no explicit revenue guidance, with commodity pass-through still dilutive.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Commodity pass-through is margin-dilutive, and employee cost and depreciation are set to rise as 16 plants ramp up, while net debt rose to Rs 2,412 crore from Rs 2,179 crore and TGJV start-up weighs on JV profit.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Pixel-based headlamp and taillamp orders from a global PV OEM, a new Japanese two-wheeler OEM seating entry, and EV charger programmes due to be commissioned in the coming quarter.

rows.label: Switch exports and four-wheeler switch ramp
rows.why: Switch exports grew significantly, rising to about Rs 218 crore from Rs 123 crore a year earlier, and the four-wheeler switch business reached Rs 617 crore, while operations shift to the expanded Faridabad facility this fiscal.

rows.label: Casting customer pipeline unverified
rows.why: Casting revenue rose 57% to Rs 1,441 crore, but management named no new casting customers, citing confidentiality, so the pipeline cannot yet be verified.

rows.label: Net debt rising with capex
rows.why: Net debt rose to Rs 2,412 crore from Rs 2,179 crore (net debt to equity 0.31) while H1 FCF after sustaining capex was Rs 404 crore and the capex pipeline is Rs 5,200-5,300 crore, so deleveraging is not in view.

tone.note: Management was confident on growth in casting, green mobility and switches and on capacity additions, but cautious on margins given aluminium pass-through dilution, and evasive on naming new casting customers; the brief does not record analyst questioning beyond the prepared Q&A topics.
